answer.value: Multimodal MoE with 552B backbone parameters; Causal Encoder-Decoder (CED): 40-layer Transformer (20-layer causal encoder, 20-layer decoder). Decoder's global KV cache is projected from final encoder hidden states, so only 8B parameters are active per token in prefill and 16B in decode, improving cost efficiency for input-heavy agentic workloads. Uses 1 shared expert and 384 routed experts per MoE layer, activating 6 routed experts per token. CSA2 assigns each attention layer one of three modes (Full, Reindex, Reuse) to share KV/indexer K and reuse Top-K indices; with FP4 main KV caching this gives 890 bytes per token global KV cache, roughly 1/4 of DeepSeek-V4-Flash.
quotes: We introduce **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash**, a multimodal Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 552B backbone parameters and support for contexts of up to one million tokens.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash adopts a **Causal Encoder-Decoder (CED)** architecture: a 40-layer Transformer organized as a 20-layer causal encoder followed by a 20-layer decoder.

With CED, the decoder's global KV cache is projected from the final encoder hidden states rather than derived from each decoder layer's own hidden states. This allows the model to activate only **8B parameters per token during prefill** and **16B during decode**, substantially improving cost efficiency for input-heavy agentic workloads.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash uses CSA2, which assigns each attention layer one of three static modes — **Full**, **Reindex**, or **Reuse** — to share main KV and indexer K across layers and reuse Top-K sparse-attention indices.

Combined with **FP4 main KV caching** (E2M1 format, one E4M3 scale per 16 channels), these designs reduce the global KV cache footprint to **890 bytes per token** — roughly **1/4** of DeepSeek-V4-Flash.
The model uses 1 shared expert and 384 routed experts per MoE layer, activating 6 routed experts per token.
